bull_bear.body: Company's focus on China plus one strategy and backward integration to drive growth and improve margins
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet leverage (Debt/Equity, including current & non-current borrowings and lease liabilities) has declined from 0.04 in FY22 to 0.00 in FY26, indicating growth funded largely without incremental debt.
- Return on Net Worth was 17.5% in FY26, down from a 24.7% peak in FY22 as the equity base and capex have scaled; EBITDA grew from INR 949 Mn (FY22) to INR 1,522 Mn (FY26) on revenue up from INR 5,301 Mn to INR 8,279 Mn.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Backward integration: 15 backward-integrated products accounting for 76% of revenue, giving control over critical inputs, cost competitiveness and supply security
- Regulatory track record across multiple jurisdictions, including a fourth USFDA approval for the Lote facility and an unannounced USFDA inspection in February 2026 that concluded with one minor observation and receipt of the Establishment Inspection Report
- Deep registration base: 50+ registrations across global markets, 21 US DMFs, 11 CEPs, 10 CADIFA (Brazil), 5 KDMF (Korea), 4 NMPA (China), 50+ ROW and 500+ customer audit approvals
- Long-standing customer relationships built on a collaborative approach, operational excellence and consistent quality, serving 1,500+ customers across 120+ countries
- Deep expertise in complex chemistries and multi-step synthesis, backed by three R&D centres (two API, one formulation) and 90 scientists
- Multi-block manufacturing infrastructure enabling therapy-wise segregation, flexibility and scalability, and the ability to manage complex chemical and high-pressure reactions
- Clear product safety profile, with no manufacture of hormones, steroids, cytotoxins, beta lactams or allergens
- Nearly four decades of pharmaceutical manufacturing experience since operations commenced at Lote in 1987
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export and geographic concentration — Exports contributed 82% of revenues during the year and Europe alone accounted for 40% of revenues, so demand, currency or trade-policy shocks in a small number of geographies transmit directly to the top line. Management explicitly cites currency volatility and evolving trade dynamics as part of the operating environment.
- Customer concentration — The top 10 customers accounted for 52% of revenue in FY 2025-26, so loss or qualification failure at a handful of accounts would be material. Management's stated counter is deepening multi-product, long-term partnerships and adding new customers across the US, Europe, LATAM, Asia-Pacific, MENA and India.
- Single-site manufacturing concentration — Production is overwhelmingly concentrated at the Lote Parshuram complex, and planned maintenance and debottlenecking at Lote depressed production in the early months of FY26. Ambernath and Patalganga are being built out partly to spread this exposure, but Lote remains the dominant asset.
- Regulatory and quality compliance risk in regulated markets — Access to the US, Europe, Canada, Brazil, China, Korea and Japan depends on maintaining USFDA, EDQM, Health Canada, ANVISA, COFEPRIS, NMPA, KFDA, PMDA and TGA approvals. The Company underwent an unannounced USFDA inspection at Lote in February 2026 which closed with one minor observation; an adverse outcome on any such inspection would restrict market access. Management notes regulatory readiness must be embedded in everyday behaviour as engagement with regulated markets expands.
- Raw material availability and input cost volatility — Management cites geopolitical conflicts, rising energy prices, supply shortages and logistics disruptions materially affecting raw material availability and input costs across the industry, plus volatility in crude and solvent prices that added to operating pressures during the year. Mitigation is backward integration (76% of revenue), strategic sourcing, alternate vendor development and disciplined inventory planning.
- Product concentration and dependence on legacy molecules — Anaesthetics alone account for 54% of segment-wise revenue contribution and remain the largest therapeutic category. Management's stated strategy is explicitly to reduce dependence on individual products and markets, and it notes that dependence on legacy products only reduces over time as newer molecules mature.
- Execution risk on the growth and diversification agenda — The FY27 revenue milestone depends on simultaneously ramping Ambernath, developing Patalganga, adding 3-4 new products a year and scaling an emerging CMO/CDMO business into formulations - a step outside the traditional API base. Management cautions that pharmaceutical growth is rarely linear and that regulatory timelines, customer qualifications, manufacturing schedules and external conditions can influence individual periods.
- Environmental, health and safety exposure of chemical manufacturing — Operations involve hazardous chemicals, high-pressure reactions, solvent handling and hazardous waste, conducted within a Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation area requiring environmental clearances. The Company runs an internal effluent treatment plant, holds authorisation under the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules 2016 and is progressively replacing hazardous materials with safer alternatives, but the exposure is structural to the business.
- Employee attrition and specialised talent dependence — The permanent-employee turnover rate was 13.37% in FY 2025-26 (down from 18.67% in FY 2024-25 and 21.00% in FY 2023-24). The business depends on 90 scientists and experienced technical teams for complex chemistry and regulatory compliance, so retention is a structural operating constraint.

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: New product launches; Capacity expansion; Regulatory approvals
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Reduce dependence on individual products and markets, expand participation in regulated geographies and create additional avenues for value creation
- Transform from a predominantly API-focused company into an integrated life sciences organisation spanning APIs, formulations and CMO/CDMO
- Add 3-4 new products every year, with FY27 additions planned across the anaesthetics and ADHD segments
- Deepen backward integration, strategic sourcing and alternate supplier development to control critical inputs and protect cost competitiveness
- Scale the CMO/CDMO business from an emerging activity into a core engine, moving from product supplier to development and manufacturing partner
- Forward integrate into dosage-form manufacturing through the formulation development and manufacturing facility at Ambernath
- R&D strategy on three axes: add niche APIs from newer therapeutic areas through sustainable processes; build capability for larger CMO/CDMO partnerships with global pharma and innovator companies; develop differentiated finished dosage products (tablets, capsules, injections, inhalation liquids) at the Ambernath formulation platform
- Deepen penetration in regulated markets through product registrations, customer qualifications and consistent regulatory compliance, with Europe and Latin America as key growth markets and expansion in the US and Japan
- Commercialise newer molecules first in markets with shorter approval cycles, then progress to more regulated geographies while registrations and customer relationships build
- Lifecycle management and cost optimisation of existing products through process innovation, yield improvement, solvent and reagent reduction, and backward integration of high-cost intermediates
- Expand capacities in line with demand: capacity additions at Lote, scale-up of Ambernath, and phased development of the Patalganga site
- Upgrade the digital architecture through automation, cloud migration to AWS, an electronic QMS (TrackWise Digital), and SAP as the next-generation ERP
- Pursue disciplined capital allocation and maintain financial flexibility, using the balance sheet as an enabler of the next growth phase
- Build long-term multi-product customer partnerships across APIs, formulations and CMO/CDMO rather than transactional relationships
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Capital expenditure during FY26 of Rs 152 crore was directed largely towards Ambernath, along with maintenance and selected expansion projects, extending the manufacturing footprint beyond the traditional API base into formulations and contract manufacturing. The CMO facility at Ambernath was commercialised in 2026, following commissioning of the state-of-the-art Module E production block at Lote Parshuram in 2025 which increased installed capacity from 597 KLPD to 932 KLPD. At Lote during FY26 the Company installed a precision distillation facility for a strategic API supporting long-term CMO opportunities, commissioned a dedicated production block for a CMO customer, added advanced solvent recovery systems, enhanced capacity for Tramadol Hydrochloride, Riboflavin Sodium Phosphate, Methylcobalamin and Nicorandil, and initiated planning for two additional production blocks to support future growth. Planned maintenance and debottlenecking at Lote affected production in the early months of the year. The Company has received the necessary clearances for the newly acquired industrial site at Isambe, Patalganga, where phased development is planned to commence in FY27, giving flexibility to add capacity in line with emerging demand while maintaining a measured approach to capital deployment. Research infrastructure has expanded with R&D labs at Lote Parshuram (2023) and Ambernath (2024), taking the Company to three R&D centres comprising two API and one formulation development centre. Looking ahead, capacity additions at Lote, the scale-up of Ambernath and the phased development of the Patalganga site are intended to provide the manufacturing platform for growth, with the operationalisation of the formulation development and manufacturing facility enabling forward integration into dosage-form manufacturing and enhancing the CMO/CDMO offering. On the technology side, the Microsoft Dynamics 365 ERP platform was migrated to the cloud, migration of domain and file server infrastructure to AWS was initiated, advanced process control automation was implemented in the E Block and is being extended to the BC Block, and SAP deployment as the next-generation ERP is targeted for completion by the beginning of FY 2027-28.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Exports contributed 82% of revenues, with Europe the largest market at 40% of revenues on higher volumes from existing customers and new customer additions
- Latin America gained significant prominence with increasing traction across both established and new products
- Backward-integrated products accounted for 76% of revenues, supporting cost competitiveness and supply reliability
- Newer products began contributing more meaningfully, with additions across cardiovascular, ADHD and liquid anaesthetics; anaesthetics further consolidated their position as the largest therapeutic category
- A key cardiovascular product launched in the third quarter commenced revenue contribution and is scaling with a robust order pipeline
- Planned maintenance and debottlenecking at Lote affected production in the early months of the year, while geopolitical events, supply-chain disruptions and volatility in crude and solvent prices added operating pressure later; momentum was restored as the year progressed
- Anaesthetics: management expects market volumes to grow at 10-15%; another anaesthetic line is expected to grow at 10-15% and products are expected to be launched in regulated markets in 2028
- Analgesics: products are expected to grow at 10-12% in markets, with new seedings initiated in the US and EU
- Anti-histamines: the Chlorpheniramine Maleate product is growing at 3-4% across all markets, with growing demand for veterinary applications, and new developments started in Vietnam and the Philippines
- Vitamins: new developments initiated in the US and Canada markets with increasing quantities from Southeast Asia and the Middle East and steady domestic demand
- Capacity utilisation at the manufacturing site stood at 74%, leaving headroom against a 100 MT per month production capacity
- Customer additions during the year across the US (7-8), Europe (5-6), Latin America (5-6), Asia-Pacific (10-11), MENA (6-7) and India (10-11)
- The external environment is expected to remain dynamic amid geopolitical uncertainties, inflationary pressures and evolving trade dynamics
- Procurement efficiency of over 90% was maintained during the year through strategic sourcing, long-term supplier partnerships and disciplined inventory management
- The successful unannounced USFDA inspection at Lote in February 2026 strengthened credentials with global customers and supports regulated-market growth
- A key cardiovascular product launched in the third quarter is now scaling with a robust order pipeline
- One CMO project has entered the commercial phase with committed production volumes extending over the next decade, while two additional projects are in advanced stages of finalisation, providing long-term business visibility
- Around 30 finished dosage products are currently under development, with multiple exhibits completed
- A novel Semaglutide tablet formulation has been developed with intellectual property filed around the differentiated formulation
- Under evaluation: exclusive manufacturing opportunities in liquid inhalation products, GLP-1 development and supply for a leading Indian generics company, and a novel combination product with an innovator partner; multiple finished dosage development and supply opportunities also under active consideration
- 50+ registrations across global markets, including 21 US DMFs, 11 CEPs, 10 CADIFA (Brazil), 5 KDMF (Korea), 4 NMPA (China) and 50+ ROW, with 500+ customer audit approvals
- Anaesthetics: a global player was tapped for contract manufacturing for their worldwide requirement, and finished dosage seeding has been established with various customers with ROW market orders expected

currentContext.expansion: Capital expenditure during FY26 of Rs 152 crore was directed largely towards Ambernath, along with maintenance and selected expansion projects, extending the manufacturing footprint beyond the traditional API base into formulations and contract manufacturing. The CMO facility at Ambernath was commercialised in 2026, following commissioning of the state-of-the-art Module E production block at Lote Parshuram in 2025 which increased installed capacity from 597 KLPD to 932 KLPD. At Lote during FY26 the Company installed a precision distillation facility for a strategic API supporting long-term CMO opportunities, commissioned a dedicated production block for a CMO customer, added advanced solvent recovery systems, enhanced capacity for Tramadol Hydrochloride, Riboflavin Sodium Phosphate, Methylcobalamin and Nicorandil, and initiated planning for two additional production blocks to support future growth. Planned maintenance and debottlenecking at Lote affected production in the early months of the year. The Company has received the necessary clearances for the newly acquired industrial site at Isambe, Patalganga, where phased development is planned to commence in FY27, giving flexibility to add capacity in line with emerging demand while maintaining a measured approach to capital deployment. Research infrastructure has expanded with R&D labs at Lote Parshuram (2023) and Ambernath (2024), taking the Company to three R&D centres comprising two API and one formulation development centre. Looking ahead, capacity additions at Lote, the scale-up of Ambernath and the phased development of the Patalganga site are intended to provide the manufacturing platform for growth, with the operationalisation of the formulation development and manufacturing facility enabling forward integration into dosage-form manufacturing and enhancing the CMO/CDMO offering. On the technology side, the Microsoft Dynamics 365 ERP platform was migrated to the cloud, migration of domain and file server infrastructure to AWS was initiated, advanced process control automation was implemented in the E Block and is being extended to the BC Block, and SAP deployment as the next-generation ERP is targeted for completion by the beginning of FY 2027-28.

risks.note: Exports contributed 82% of revenues during the year and Europe alone accounted for 40% of revenues, so demand, currency or trade-policy shocks in a small number of geographies transmit directly to the top line. Management explicitly cites currency volatility and evolving trade dynamics as part of the operating environment.

The top 10 customers accounted for 52% of revenue in FY 2025-26, so loss or qualification failure at a handful of accounts would be material. Management's stated counter is deepening multi-product, long-term partnerships and adding new customers across the US, Europe, LATAM, Asia-Pacific, MENA and India.

Production is overwhelmingly concentrated at the Lote Parshuram complex, and planned maintenance and debottlenecking at Lote depressed production in the early months of FY26. Ambernath and Patalganga are being built out partly to spread this exposure, but Lote remains the dominant asset.

risks.risk: Regulatory and quality compliance risk in regulated markets
risks.note: Access to the US, Europe, Canada, Brazil, China, Korea and Japan depends on maintaining USFDA, EDQM, Health Canada, ANVISA, COFEPRIS, NMPA, KFDA, PMDA and TGA approvals. The Company underwent an unannounced USFDA inspection at Lote in February 2026 which closed with one minor observation; an adverse outcome on any such inspection would restrict market access. Management notes regulatory readiness must be embedded in everyday behaviour as engagement with regulated markets expands.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and input cost volatility
risks.note: Management cites geopolitical conflicts, rising energy prices, supply shortages and logistics disruptions materially affecting raw material availability and input costs across the industry, plus volatility in crude and solvent prices that added to operating pressures during the year. Mitigation is backward integration (76% of revenue), strategic sourcing, alternate vendor development and disciplined inventory planning.

risks.risk: Product concentration and dependence on legacy molecules
risks.note: Anaesthetics alone account for 54% of segment-wise revenue contribution and remain the largest therapeutic category. Management's stated strategy is explicitly to reduce dependence on individual products and markets, and it notes that dependence on legacy products only reduces over time as newer molecules mature.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the growth and diversification agenda
risks.note: The FY27 revenue milestone depends on simultaneously ramping Ambernath, developing Patalganga, adding 3-4 new products a year and scaling an emerging CMO/CDMO business into formulations - a step outside the traditional API base. Management cautions that pharmaceutical growth is rarely linear and that regulatory timelines, customer qualifications, manufacturing schedules and external conditions can influence individual periods.

risks.risk: Environmental, health and safety exposure of chemical manufacturing
risks.note: Operations involve hazardous chemicals, high-pressure reactions, solvent handling and hazardous waste, conducted within a Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation area requiring environmental clearances. The Company runs an internal effluent treatment plant, holds authorisation under the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules 2016 and is progressively replacing hazardous materials with safer alternatives, but the exposure is structural to the business.

risks.risk: Employee attrition and specialised talent dependence
risks.note: The permanent-employee turnover rate was 13.37% in FY 2025-26 (down from 18.67% in FY 2024-25 and 21.00% in FY 2023-24). The business depends on 90 scientists and experienced technical teams for complex chemistry and regulatory compliance, so retention is a structural operating constraint.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Supriya Lifescience is a Mumbai-headquartered global life sciences company developing and manufacturing niche Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, formulations and CMO/CDMO solutions, serving over 1,500 customers across 120+ countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1987 as a partnership firm and incorporated as a public limited company in 2008, the Company develops and manufactures niche Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and is extending into formulations and CMO/CDMO solutions. It offers a portfolio of 40+ specialised APIs spanning anaesthetics, antihistamines, analgesics, vitamins, anti-asthmatics and anti-allergics, sold to innovator companies, generic formulation manufacturers and traders worldwide. Manufacturing is concentrated at Lote Parshuram in Ratnagiri, Maharashtra, with a newer site at Ambernath, supported by three R&D centres and a backward-integrated business model.

- **Antihistamines:** Chlorpheniramine Maleate, Brompheniramine Maleate, Pheniramine Maleate, Mepyramine Maleate, Cetirizine Dihydrochloride, Diphenhydramine
- **Analgesics:** Tramadol Hydrochloride, Ibuprofen Picanol
- **Vitamins:** Riboflavin Sodium Phosphate, Methylcobalamin
- **Anti-asthmatics:** Salbutamol Sulphate
- **Cardiovascular / anti-hypertensive:** Nicorandil, Bisoprolol Fumarate, ATS-8 (Atorvastatin Calcium Intermediate)

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

hero.oneLiner: Supriya Lifescience is a Mumbai-headquartered global life sciences company developing and manufacturing niche Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, formulations and CMO/CDMO solutions, serving over 1,500 customers across 120+ countries.
